chapter.title: Space and Science
chapter.description: Our corner of the universe, and the physics that runs it.

parts.title: The Solar System
parts.description: Surprising facts about our Sun and its planets.

cards.title: Sunlight is about 8 minutes old
cards.body:
Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.

So when you look at the Sun (please don't, directly), you're seeing it as it was a little over eight minutes ago.

cards.title: 1 AU ≈ 150 million km
cards.body:
Astronomers measure distances in the Solar System with the astronomical unit, or AU: roughly the average distance from Earth to the Sun, about 150 million kilometers.

Jupiter is about 5 AU from the Sun. Neptune is about 30 AU.

cards.title: The hottest planet isn't the closest
cards.body:
Mercury is closest to the Sun, but Venus is the hottest planet, with surface temperatures around 465°C.

Venus has a thick atmosphere made mostly of carbon dioxide. It traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect, hot enough to melt lead.

cards.title: Seasons come from the tilt
cards.body:
Earth's axis is tilted about 23.4 degrees. As Earth orbits, first one hemisphere and then the other leans toward the Sun, getting more direct sunlight and longer days.

Seasons aren't caused by distance. Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January, during northern winter.

cards.title: Jupiter outweighs everyone
cards.body:
Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

It is mostly hydrogen and helium, and its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth.

cards.title: A day longer than a year
cards.body:
Venus spins very slowly, and backwards compared with most planets. One full rotation takes about 243 Earth days, while one trip around the Sun takes about 225.

So on Venus, a day (one rotation) is longer than a year.

cards.title: Why Pluto was reclassified
cards.body:
In 2006, the International Astronomical Union defined a planet as a body that orbits the Sun, is round from its own gravity, and has cleared its orbit of other material.

Pluto meets the first two but shares its region with many icy objects in the Kuiper Belt. So it became a dwarf planet.

questions.question: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
Why is Venus hotter than Mercury?
options: Venus is closer to the Sun
Its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat
questions.explanation: A runaway greenhouse effect keeps Venus around 465°C.

questions.question: What causes Earth's seasons?
options: Changes in Earth's distance from the Sun
questions.explanation: A tilt of about 23.4° changes how directly sunlight hits each hemisphere.

questions.question: Why is Pluto classed as a dwarf planet?
options: It hasn't cleared its orbit of other objects
questions.explanation: Pluto shares its orbital region with other Kuiper Belt objects.

questions.question: On which planet is a day longer than a year?
questions.explanation: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once but about 225 to orbit the Sun.

parts.title: How rockets work
parts.description: Pushing against nothing, and getting to orbit.

cards.title: Throw stuff backward, go forward
cards.body:
A rocket doesn't push against the air. It throws hot gas out of its nozzle very fast, and the gas pushes the rocket the other way, which is Newton's third law.

Rockets also carry their own oxidizer along with fuel, so they can burn in the vacuum of space where there's no air.

cards.title: 299,792 kilometers per second
cards.body:
That's the speed of light in a vacuum, about 300,000 km every second. Light could circle Earth about seven and a half times in one second.

The meter is now defined using this speed, which is set at exactly 299,792,458 meters per second.
